explainer.heading: This is no longer acne — it is pigment left behind after the inflammation ended
body: When a spot becomes inflamed, the skin responds by producing more melanin in that area. The spot settles, the melanin does not, and it leaves on pigment's timescale — weeks and months, not days.

Which explains two things. First, a product made for acne does nothing for a mark, because there is no acne left to act on. Second, squeezing makes the mark deeper and longer-lasting, because it drives the damage further down and prolongs the inflammation.
And because this is pigment, sun darkens it exactly as it darkens melasma. A mark kept out of the sun fades noticeably faster than the same mark exposed daily.

blocks.heading: Three kinds of post-acne mark, and which one this tube addresses
blocks.intro: Not every mark left by acne is the same thing. Telling them apart first saves both money and time.

items.heading: Flat brown marks
items.body: Pigment left after inflammation, with the skin surface still smooth. This is what the tube was made for.

items.heading: Flat red or pink marks
items.body: Dilated vessels left after inflammation, not melanin. These usually fade on their own; brightening actives do little. Moisturising and sun protection do the work.

items.heading: Indented or raised scars
items.body: A change in the structure of the skin, not in its pigment. No topical product fills an indented scar — that needs a clinic.

items.q: How long until I see a difference?
items.a: We do not quote a figure. Post-blemish marks sit at very different depths depending on how inflamed things were, so one shared timescale would be wrong for most readers. What is more certain: without sun protection the marks darken faster than any product can soften them.

items.q: How is it different from Smart Brightening Cream?
items.a: The active families overlap — both carry tranexamic acid and niacinamide. They differ in format and area: this is a 20g gel for marks left after blemishes, the cream is 30g for the whole face over a longer routine.

items.q: Can I use it on an active breakout?
items.a: Not the right moment. This is the step after the spot has settled. Inflamed areas need something else.
Keep away from heat and direct sunlight, close after use, keep out of reach of children.
